Test the three unverified assumptions first.

worker/index.js + worker/dev.js (dev login absent from prod entry)

log.msg: assumption 1 VERIFIED: wrangler dev -c wrangler.dev.jsonc --port 8787 and PORT=8092 node server.js coexist fine, both serving requests concurrently, no port/file-lock conflict on Windows

assumption 2 VERIFIED (noise only): a WS upgrade to ws://localhost:8787/ (the framework dev Socket's target) is not a route the worker handles, falls through to ASSETS.fetch, which returns a plain 200 HTML page instead of a 101 - the ws client sees this as unexpected-response/error+close, matching Socket.js's existing backoff-reconnect path. No page breakage.

assumption 3 VERIFIED: a session cookie (HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Lax) set at http://localhost:8787 IS included on a WebSocket handshake to ws://localhost:8787 opened from a page whose own origin is http://localhost:8092 (RFC 6265 SS8.5, cookies not port-scoped) - confirmed with a real Chromium context, not just a claim. Also confirmed Secure cookies persist fine over plain http://localhost. The harness still uses one origin (design already chose this), but the fallback claim holds if ever needed.

BUG FOUND while testing: wrangler 4.129 warns 'Unexpected fields found in top-level field: run_worker_first' when it sits at wrangler.dev.jsonc top level (as local-dev.md's file table shows it) - and worse, it is then SILENTLY IGNORED: a navigation-style GET (Sec-Fetch-Dest: document, the header a real <a href> or page.goto() sends) to /api/dev/login was served the SPA-fallback index.html (200) instead of reaching the worker, because not_found_handling:'single-page-application' wins for navigations when run_worker_first isn't recognized. Fix: nest it under assets - assets.run_worker_first: ["/api/*"] - which wrangler accepts with no warning and correctly routes navigations too. This would have silently broken every dev-login link (the room test's exact login gesture) had it shipped as documented.

assign.outcome:
**The local multi-user harness runs — `npm run dev`, one command, real identity and a real Durable Object room, fully local.** All three unverified assumptions from [`local-dev.md`](/imagine/platform/decisions/local-dev.md) held (wrangler+node coexistence, dev-socket noise-only, cookie on a cross-port WS) — tested with a real Chromium context each, not asserted. Testing them also caught a real bug: `run_worker_first` at the config's top level is silently ignored by wrangler 4.129, and a plain navigation to `/api/dev/login` fell through to the SPA fallback instead of the worker — fixed by nesting it under `assets`. The room test passed 4/4 on the first real run: bob sees alice's message within 2s, eve (banned) refused at connect, anonymous reads but the composer disables itself.

![alice and bob, same message, two tabs](room-test-bob.png)

Cut: role/ban live in the session payload (a dev-only handle→role map), not new D1 columns — `identity.md` ruling 7 keeps the `users` table exactly `/notes/auth/` §4; no mid-room mute, no KV ban key (production-only); no compaction alarm. `public/imagine/platform/local/` is not yet linked from `platform/page.js`'s `children:` — the brief reserves that wire for the mastermind.
